_note: The ADR-0035 §8 lineages. Each is pre-trained from scratch by pipeline.py under one profile. Seeds differ on purpose: two lineages with the same family, preset, vocabulary and seed start from byte-identical weights, so they share a root and E1 fails, correctly. `tokenizer_from` and `init_from` name another lineage in this file.

smoke._note: Pipeline check only: 1M params, 5M tokens, 20 MB per corpus. Minutes per lineage; the samples are noise.

small._note: Every lineage in ~20 min on an M4 Pro (10M params, 50M tokens). Enough to exercise the whole pipeline and the table; not enough for good samples.

full._note: The session's range: 30M params at Chinchilla-optimal 550M tokens, ~7 h each on an M4 Pro (bench.py measures yours). Eight lineages ≈ 2.5 days of GPU time; run them one at a time under run_long.sh.

L-A.expect: pass pair with L-B; E1 with L-A'; E3 (+E5) with L-C; E4 with L-D; E5 with L-E5

L-A-prime.expect: E1 with L-A: a fine-tune of L-A on books

L-C.expect: E3 with L-A. FineWeb-Edu's rows are FineWeb's rows after filtering, in the same order, so a FineWeb head slice ~12x the FineWeb-Edu slice contains it entirely (measured: 3,911 of 3,911 documents). E5 fires too: both carry FineWeb's language-ID curator

L-D.expect: E4 alone with L-A: same family, while E3 passes

L-T.expect: distillation: provenance rung 1 (content from GPT-3.5 and GPT-4)

L-T2.expect: E2 with L-T: synthetic sets naming a common generator

L-E5.expect: E5 with L-A: corpora filtered by the same classifier
